zh_summary: so $SPCX obviously blew the doors out with those earnings especially if Elon gets anywhere close to his goal of bringing 20GW online by next year. The question now seems to be what this means for every other neocloud. SpaceX is up today, the rest are flat to red. On one hand, $SPCX proved how important the neocloud business model is and how much demand is out there. On the other hand, $SPCX was so good that now people are doubting the ability for other neoclouds to easily finance their operations, how quickly those companies can bring compute online compared to Elon, and how much debt/dilution SpaceX themselves will have to take on to finance that buildout which then begs the question around how much dilution the smaller players will have to take on. SpaceX is also profitable whereas the others are years from profitability. My take is more that $SPCX has validated the entire concept of neoclouds which obviously have been under stress given the $CRWV bonds getting hit over the past two weeks, but the earnings were also so good that there might be more questions now about how well the others can execute. The broader theme seemed to be legitimized from those earnings: the compute constraints exist and have not eased up in any meaningful way.

The remaining 485 stocks represent just 53.3%  of the S&P 500’s market cap.

Furthermore, the combined market cap of the 5 largest stocks now equals that of the bottom 434 stocks in the index, the largest gap on record.

Market concentration is at historic extremes.

October hands traders a dip almost every year. So do midterm years. In 2026 they land on the same calendar, and some of the most valuable companies on Earth are trading well off their highs 

THE CRASHES
1929: Dow -12.8% on Oct 28, then -11.7% the next day
1987: Dow -22.6% on Black Monday, still its worst day ever
2008: S&P -16.9% for the month as the Lehman fallout spread

A speculative bubble, a market-structure meltdown, a credit crisis. Different causes, same month, and every one of them eventually became a buying window

THE OCTOBER STATS
Typical recovery: about 4 months
Midterm Octobers: +3.0% average, green 73.7% of the time

Nobody buys the exact low, and nobody needs to. Every rebound $SPX has historically paid the people who kept buying good names on the way down

SCENARIOS
Bullish Scenario: $SPX holds 7600 heading into the Nov 3 midterms. Bulls can look for a push towards 7800 by mid-November, with a breakout to new ATHs opening the door towards 8000-8100. The biggest clue will be continued strength in market leaders $NBIS $SNDK $MU $DELL $AMD. As long as these names continue printing higher lows and outperforming the broader market, bulls remain in control.

Bearish Scenario: $SPX loses 7600 heading into Nov 3, opening the door for a deeper pullback towards 7400-7500. Rather than blindly buying the dip, look for aggressive selling, rising fear, and signs of capitulation as price approaches support. T
